title: Zoom in: the hybrid read builds one page from two sources
caption: Most of the page is precomputed; only the handful of big accounts a reader follows is fetched and merged per request.

steps.text: Read the reader's newest timeline ids: one key, a few hundred ids.
It is in cache, so take the list of big accounts this reader follows (stored next to the timeline).
They follow a few: fetch each one's recent post ids, a handful of small reads that run in parallel.
Merge both lists by time and keep the newest page.
Hydrate post bodies in one multi-get and drop deleted posts and blocked authors, then return.

scenarios.name: Cold timeline
scenarios.summary: A user returns after months away and their timeline was evicted: rebuild it once by pulling, then they are back on the fast path.

steps.text: The timeline key is gone; inactive users' timelines are evicted to save memory.
Pull the recent posts of the people they follow, merge, and write the result back as their timeline. This one open is slow (~300 ms).
Continue as usual with the big accounts and hydration.

scenarios.name: Big-account fetch times out
scenarios.summary: Degrade, don't fail: serve the pushed part of the page and let the next refresh fill in the big accounts.

steps.text: Timeline read and big-accounts list as usual.
The fetch of big accounts' recent posts exceeds its 50 ms budget.
Merge only what we have and return the page; a metric counts the degraded responses.

scenarios.name: Deleted post
scenarios.summary: The author deleted a post after it was pushed to a million timelines. Don't chase the copies; filter at read time.

steps.text: The post id is still in many timelines; removing it everywhere would be another million writes.
Hydration finds a tombstone for that id and drops it, then fills the page from the next ids.
The reader never sees it; the stale id falls off the capped timeline eventually.
